title: Here’s what happened in crypto today

title: Democrat backed by Ripple co-founder’s PAC wins Colorado primary
summary: Colorado’s Democratic and Republican primaries finished on Tuesday, with at least one candidate supported by $1 million from a crypto-aligned PAC going to the November general election.

title: Bitcoin bear market ‘dead’ after first TD9 reversal signal since July 2022 fires
summary: Bitcoin bear-market bottom signs appear as the TD9 indicator mirrors the final stages of the 2022 BTC price downtrend.

title: Crypto ATM bans, restrictions now in effect in Tennessee and Georgia
summary: Crypto ATM's are fast disappearing in the US as Tennessee’s ban goes into effect today while operators in Minnesota have until Aug. 1 to comply with a similar law.

title: Anchorage Digital brings off-exchange settlement to Binance
summary: The integration addresses one of the biggest obstacles keeping institutional capital on the sidelines of crypto markets: exchange counterparty risk.

title: Bitcoin price returns to $60K as US dollar strength rejects weekly high
summary: Bitcoin started July with a bang, rallying above $60,000 as traders predict a relief rally as the “base case” throughout the month.

title: Ethereum backers launch nonprofit to lead institutional adoption efforts
summary: Backed by Joe Lubin, BitMine and SharpLink, the independent organization will serve as a liaison for financial institutions exploring Ethereum as competition for institutional capital heats up.

title: French banking giant Crédit Agricole launches EURXT euro stablecoin
summary: Crédit Agricole’s CACEIS launches a euro-pegged stablecoin on Ethereum with 20.02 million tokens issued, targeting institutional flows and tokenized fund access.

title: Bank of Korea governor outlines tokenized bond vision, unified ledger plan
summary: The Bank of Korea’s governor praised tokenized government bonds for easing the issuance and management of government debt during a panel discussion at the ECB Forum.

title: Circle CEO touts USDC's network advantage as OUSD emerges
